original: No act or proceeding of the Central Authority shall be invalid merely by reason of— (a) any vacancy in, or any defect in the constitution of, the Central Authority; or (b) any defect in the appointment of a person acting as the Chief Commissioner or as a Commissioner; or (c) any irregularity in the procedure of the Central Authority not affecting the merits of the case.
simplification: The Central Authority's decisions still count even if a seat is empty or there was a small mistake in how someone was appointed.

original: No act or proceeding of the Central Authority shall be invalid merely by reason of— (a) any vacancy in, or any defect in the constitution of, the Central Authority; or (b) any defect in the appointment of a person acting as the Chief Commissioner or as a Commissioner; or (c) any irregularity in the procedure of the Central Authority not affecting the merits of the case.
simplification: No action or proceeding of the Central Authority will become invalid just because of: (a) a vacancy in, or a defect in how the Central Authority was formed; (b) a defect in the appointment of a person acting as Chief Commissioner or Commissioner; or (c) any irregularity in its procedure that does not affect the merits of the case.

original: No act or proceeding of the Central Authority shall be invalid merely by reason of— (a) any vacancy in, or any defect in the constitution of, the Central Authority; or (b) any defect in the appointment of a person acting as the Chief Commissioner or as a Commissioner; or (c) any irregularity in the procedure of the Central Authority not affecting the merits of the case.
simplification: No action or proceeding of the Central Authority will become invalid just because of: (a) a vacancy in, or a defect in how the Central Authority was formed; (b) a defect in the appointment of a person acting as Chief Commissioner or Commissioner; or (c) certain irregularity in its procedure that does not affect the merits of the case.

original: A person aggrieved by any order passed by the Central Authority under sections 20 and 21 may file an appeal to the National Commission within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of such order.
simplification: If you don't agree with a decision of the Central Authority, you can complain to the National Commission within 30 days.

original: A person aggrieved by any order passed by the Central Authority under sections 20 and 21 may file an appeal to the National Commission within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of such order.
simplification: A person unhappy with an order made by the Central Authority under sections 20 and 21 can appeal to the National Commission within thirty days of receiving the order.

original: A person aggrieved by any order passed by the Central Authority under sections 20 and 21 may file an appeal to the National Commission within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of such order.

original: The State Government shall provide the District Commission with such officers and other employees as may be required to assist the District Commission in the discharge of its functions.
simplification: The state government has to give the District Commission enough workers to help it.

simplification: The State Government may give the District Commission the officers and staff it needs to help it do its work.

original: On receipt of a complaint made under section 35, the District Commission may, by order, admit the complaint for being proceeded with or reject the same: Provided that a complaint shall not be rejected under this section unless an opportunity of being heard has been given to the complainant: Provided further that the admissibility of the complaint shall ordinarily be decided within twenty-one days from the date on which the complaint was filed.
simplification: When you file a consumer complaint, the District Commission decides whether to take it up, usually within 21 days. It has to listen to you before saying no.

original: On receipt of a complaint made under section 35, the District Commission may, by order, admit the complaint for being proceeded with or reject the same: Provided that a complaint shall not be rejected under this section unless an opportunity of being heard has been given to the complainant: Provided further that the admissibility of the complaint shall ordinarily be decided within twenty-one days from the date on which the complaint was filed.
simplification: When the District Commission receives a complaint under section 35, it may accept the complaint so that it can go ahead, or reject it. However, a complaint cannot be rejected unless the complainant has been given a chance to be heard. Also, the decision on whether to accept the complaint should usually be made within twenty-one days from the date it was filed.

original: On receipt of a complaint made under section 35, the District Commission may, by order, admit the complaint for being proceeded with or reject the same: Provided that a complaint shall not be rejected under this section unless an opportunity of being heard has been given to the complainant: Provided further that the admissibility of the complaint shall ordinarily be decided within twenty-one days from the date on which the complaint was filed.
simplification: When the District Commission receives a complaint under section 35, it may accept the complaint so that it can go ahead, or reject it. original: Where the District Commission does not decide the issue of admissibility of the complaint within the period so specified, it shall be deemed to have been admitted.
simplification: If the District Commission doesn't decide in time, your complaint is accepted automatically.

original: Where the District Commission does not decide the issue of admissibility of the complaint within the period so specified, it shall be deemed to have been admitted.

original: Where the District Commission does not decide the issue of admissibility of the complaint within the period so specified, it shall be deemed to have been admitted.
simplification: If the District Commission does decide whether to admit the complaint within the set time, the complaint will be treated as admitted.

original: Where the parties agree for settlement by mediation and give their consent in writing, the District Commission shall, within five days of receipt of such consent, refer the matter for mediation, and in such case, the provisions of Chapter V, relating to mediation, shall apply.
simplification: If both sides agree in writing to talk it out, the District Commission sends the case to mediation within 5 days.

original: Where the parties agree for settlement by mediation and give their consent in writing, the District Commission shall, within five days of receipt of such consent, refer the matter for mediation, and in such case, the provisions of Chapter V, relating to mediation, shall apply.
simplification: If the parties agree to settle by mediation and give their consent in writing, the District Commission must send the matter for mediation within five days of getting that consent. In that case, the rules on mediation in Chapter V will apply.

original: Where the parties agree for settlement by mediation and give their consent in writing, the District Commission shall, within five days of receipt of such consent, refer the matter for mediation, and in such case, the provisions of Chapter V, relating to mediation, shall apply.
simplification: If the parties agree to settle by mediation and give their consent in writing, the District Commission must send the matter for mediation within ten days of getting that consent. In that case, the rules on mediation in Chapter V will apply.

original: Every complaint shall be heard by the District Commission on the basis of affidavit and documentary evidence placed on record: Provided that where an application is made for hearing or for examination of parties in person or through video conferencing, the District Commission may, on sufficient cause being shown, and after recording its reasons in writing, allow the same.
simplification: The District Commission mostly decides cases by reading written statements and papers. Sometimes it can let people speak in person or on video.

original: Every complaint shall be heard by the District Commission on the basis of affidavit and documentary evidence placed on record: Provided that where an application is made for hearing or for examination of parties in person or through video conferencing, the District Commission may, on sufficient cause being shown, and after recording its reasons in writing, allow the same.
simplification: The District Commission will hear every complaint based on affidavits and documents on record. However, if someone applies to be heard or to have the parties examined in person or by video conference, the District Commission may allow it if there is a good reason and it writes down its reasons.

original: Every complaint shall be heard by the District Commission on the basis of affidavit and documentary evidence placed on record: Provided that where an application is made for hearing or for examination of parties in person or through video conferencing, the District Commission may, on sufficient cause being shown, and after recording its reasons in writing, allow the same.
simplification: The District Commission will hear every complaint based on affidavits and documents on record.

original: The Central Government shall, by notification, establish with effect from such date as it may specify in that notification, the Central Consumer Protection Council to be known as the Central Council.
simplification: The central government will create a group called the Central Council to look after consumers.

original: The Central Government shall, by notification, establish with effect from such date as it may specify in that notification, the Central Consumer Protection Council to be known as the Central Council.

original: The Central Government shall, by notification, establish with effect from such date as it may specify in that notification, the Central Consumer Protection Council to be known as the Central Council.
simplification: The Central Government will not set up the Central Consumer Protection Council, called the Central Council, by a notification, starting from the date given in that notification.

original: Save as otherwise expressly provided under this Act or by any other law for the time being in force, an appeal shall lie to the National Commission from any order passed in appeal by any State Commission, if the National Commission is satisfied that the case involves a substantial question of law.
simplification: If a State Commission decides an appeal, you can go to the National Commission next. It will only take the case if there is an important legal question.

original: Save as otherwise expressly provided under this Act or by any other law for the time being in force, an appeal shall lie to the National Commission from any order passed in appeal by any State Commission, if the National Commission is satisfied that the case involves a substantial question of law.
simplification: Unless this Act or another law in force clearly says otherwise, an appeal can be made to the National Commission against any order that a State Commission passed in an appeal, if the National Commission is satisfied that the case raises a substantial question of law.

original: Save as otherwise expressly provided under this Act or by any other law for the time being in force, an appeal shall lie to the National Commission from any order passed in appeal by any State Commission, if the National Commission is satisfied that the case involves a substantial question of law.
simplification: An appeal can be made to the National Commission against any order that a State Commission passed in an appeal, if the National Commission is satisfied that the case raises a substantial question of law.

original: Where the National Commission is satisfied that a substantial question of law is involved in any case, it shall formulate that question and hear the appeal on that question: Provided that nothing in this sub-section shall be deemed to take away or abridge the power of the National Commission to hear, for reasons to be recorded in writing, the appeal on any other substantial question of law, if it is satisfied that the case involves such question of law.
simplification: The National Commission writes down the main legal question in a case and hears the appeal on it. It can also look at other important legal questions if it explains why.

original: Where the National Commission is satisfied that a substantial question of law is involved in any case, it shall formulate that question and hear the appeal on that question: Provided that nothing in this sub-section shall be deemed to take away or abridge the power of the National Commission to hear, for reasons to be recorded in writing, the appeal on any other substantial question of law, if it is satisfied that the case involves such question of law.
simplification: If the National Commission is satisfied that a case involves a substantial question of law, it must state that question and hear the appeal on it. However, this does not stop the National Commission from hearing the appeal on another substantial question of law, if it finds that the case involves one and writes down its reasons.

original: Where the National Commission is satisfied that a substantial question of law is involved in any case, it shall formulate that question and hear the appeal on that question: Provided that nothing in this sub-section shall be deemed to take away or abridge the power of the National Commission to hear, for reasons to be recorded in writing, the appeal on any other substantial question of law, if it is satisfied that the case involves such question of law.
simplification: If the National Commission is satisfied that a case involves a substantial question of law, it must state that question and hear the appeal on it.

original: The jurisdiction, powers and authority of the National Commission may be exercised by Benches thereof and a Bench may be constituted by the President with one or more members as he may deem fit: Provided that the senior-most member of the Bench shall preside over the Bench.
simplification: The National Commission can split into smaller groups to hear cases. The most senior member leads each group.

original: The jurisdiction, powers and authority of the National Commission may be exercised by Benches thereof and a Bench may be constituted by the President with one or more members as he may deem fit: Provided that the senior-most member of the Bench shall preside over the Bench.
simplification: The National Commission can use its jurisdiction, powers and authority through its Benches. The President can form a Bench with one or more members as he thinks fit, and the most senior member of the Bench will lead it.

original: The jurisdiction, powers and authority of the National Commission may be exercised by Benches thereof and a Bench may be constituted by the President with one or more members as he may deem fit: Provided that the senior-most member of the Bench shall preside over the Bench.
simplification: The National Commission can use its jurisdiction, powers and authority through its Benches. The President must form a Bench with one or more members as he thinks fit, and the most senior member of the Bench will lead it.

original: Without prejudice to the provisions contained in sub-section (1), the notice required by this Act may be served on an electronic service provider at the address provided by it on the electronic platform from where it provides its services as such and for this purpose, the electronic service provider shall designate a nodal officer to accept and process such notices.
simplification: Online companies can be sent legal notices at the address they show on their website or app. They must name an officer to deal with these notices.

original: Without prejudice to the provisions contained in sub-section (1), the notice required by this Act may be served on an electronic service provider at the address provided by it on the electronic platform from where it provides its services as such and for this purpose, the electronic service provider shall designate a nodal officer to accept and process such notices.
simplification: In addition to sub-section (1), a notice required under this Act may be sent to an electronic service provider at the address it gives on the online platform where it offers its services. For this, the electronic service provider must appoint a nodal officer to receive and handle such notices.

original: Without prejudice to the provisions contained in sub-section (1), the notice required by this Act may be served on an electronic service provider at the address provided by it on the electronic platform from where it provides its services as such and for this purpose, the electronic service provider shall designate a nodal officer to accept and process such notices.
simplification: In addition to sub-section (1), a notice required under this Act must be sent to an electronic service provider at the address it gives on the online platform where it offers its services. For this, the electronic service provider must appoint a nodal officer to receive and handle such notices.

original: Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), a complaint may be entertained after the period specified in sub-section (1), if the complainant satisfies the District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, that he had sufficient cause for not filing the complaint within such period: Provided that no such complaint shall be entertained unless the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, records its reasons for condoning such delay.
simplification: If you file a consumer complaint late, it can still be accepted if you had a good reason. The commission has to write down why it is allowing it.

original: Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), a complaint may be entertained after the period specified in sub-section (1), if the complainant satisfies the District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, that he had sufficient cause for not filing the complaint within such period: Provided that no such complaint shall be entertained unless the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, records its reasons for condoning such delay.
simplification: Even though sub-section (1) sets a time limit, a complaint can still be accepted after that period if the complainant shows the District, State or National Commission that there was a good reason for the delay. But the Commission must write down its reasons for excusing the delay before accepting such a complaint.

original: Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), a complaint may be entertained after the period specified in sub-section (1), if the complainant satisfies the District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, that he had sufficient cause for not filing the complaint within such period: Provided that no such complaint shall be entertained unless the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, records its reasons for condoning such delay.
simplification: Even though sub-section (1) sets a time limit, a complaint can still be accepted after that period if the complainant shows the District, State or National Commission that there was a good reason for the delay.

original: The State Council shall be an advisory council and consist of the following members, namely:— (a) the Minister-in-charge of Consumer Affairs in the State Government who shall be the Chairperson; (b) such number of other official or non-official members representing such interests as may be prescribed; (c) such number of other official or non-official members, not exceeding ten, as may be nominated by the Central Government.
simplification: The State Council gives advice and is led by the state's consumer affairs minister. It also has other members, including up to ten picked by the central government.

original: The State Council shall be an advisory council and consist of the following members, namely:— (a) the Minister-in-charge of Consumer Affairs in the State Government who shall be the Chairperson; (b) such number of other official or non-official members representing such interests as may be prescribed; (c) such number of other official or non-official members, not exceeding ten, as may be nominated by the Central Government.
simplification: The State Council will be an advisory council with these members: (a) the State Minister in charge of Consumer Affairs, who will be the Chairperson; (b) a prescribed number of other official or non-official members representing certain interests; and (c) up to ten other official or non-official members nominated by the Central Government.

original: The State Council shall be an advisory council and consist of the following members, namely:— (a) the Minister-in-charge of Consumer Affairs in the State Government who shall be the Chairperson; (b) such number of other official or non-official members representing such interests as may be prescribed; (c) such number of other official or non-official members, not exceeding ten, as may be nominated by the Central Government.
simplification: The State Council will be an advisory council with these members: (a) the State Minister in charge of Consumer Affairs, who will not be the Chairperson; (b) a prescribed number of other official or non-official members representing certain interests; and (c) up to ten other official or non-official members nominated by the Central Government.

original: Every order made by a District Commission, State Commission or the National Commission shall be enforced by it in the same manner as if it were a decree made by a Court in a suit before it and the provisions of Order XXI of the First Schedule to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 shall, as far as may be, applicable, subject to the modification that every reference therein to the decree shall be construed as reference to the order made under this Act.
simplification: When a consumer commission makes a decision, it must be followed just like a court's decision.

original: Every order made by a District Commission, State Commission or the National Commission shall be enforced by it in the same manner as if it were a decree made by a Court in a suit before it and the provisions of Order XXI of the First Schedule to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 shall, as far as may be, applicable, subject to the modification that every reference therein to the decree shall be construed as reference to the order made under this Act.
simplification: Every order made by a District Commission, State Commission or the National Commission will be enforced by that Commission as if it were a court decree in a civil suit. original: Every order made by a District Commission, State Commission or the National Commission shall be enforced by it in the same manner as if it were a decree made by a Court in a suit before it and the provisions of Order XXI of the First Schedule to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 shall, as far as may be, applicable, subject to the modification that every reference therein to the decree shall be construed as reference to the order made under this Act.
simplification: Some order made by a District Commission, State Commission or the National Commission will be enforced by that Commission as if it were a court decree in a civil suit. original: Save as otherwise provided, the offences under sub-section (1) shall be tried summarily by the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be.

original: Save as otherwise provided, the offences under sub-section (1) shall be tried summarily by the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be.
simplification: Unless stated otherwise, the District, State or National Commission will try the offences under sub-section (1) in a summary (quick) way.

original: Save as otherwise provided, the offences under sub-section (1) shall be tried summarily by the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be.
simplification: The District, State or National Commission will try the offences under sub-section (1) in a summary (quick) way.

original: The State Government shall establish, by notification, a consumer mediation cell to be attached to each of the District Commissions and the State Commissions of that State.
simplification: Each state must create a special team at every consumer commission to help both sides settle their problems.

original: The State Government shall establish, by notification, a consumer mediation cell to be attached to each of the District Commissions and the State Commissions of that State.

simplification: The State Government must set up, by notification, a consumer mediation cell attached to some District Commission and State Commission in the State.

original: For the purpose of mediation, the National Commission or the State Commission or the District Commission, as the case may be, shall prepare a panel of the mediators to be maintained by the consumer mediation cell attached to it, on the recommendation of a selection committee consisting of the President and a member of that Commission.
simplification: Each consumer commission keeps a list of people who can help both sides agree. A small committee picks these people.

original: For the purpose of mediation, the National Commission or the State Commission or the District Commission, as the case may be, shall prepare a panel of the mediators to be maintained by the consumer mediation cell attached to it, on the recommendation of a selection committee consisting of the President and a member of that Commission.
simplification: For mediation, the National, State or District Commission will prepare a panel of mediators, kept by the consumer mediation cell attached to it. The panel is made on the advice of a selection committee made up of the President and a member of that Commission.

original: For the purpose of mediation, the National Commission or the State Commission or the District Commission, as the case may be, shall prepare a panel of the mediators to be maintained by the consumer mediation cell attached to it, on the recommendation of a selection committee consisting of the President and a member of that Commission.
simplification: For mediation, the National, State or District Commission will not prepare a panel of mediators, kept by the consumer mediation cell attached to it. The panel is made on the advice of a selection committee made up of the President and a member of that Commission.

original: Where the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, is satisfied, on the information furnished by the mediator or on the information received from any other person including parties to the complaint and after hearing the mediator, it shall replace such mediator by another mediator.
simplification: If there is a problem with a mediator, the consumer commission will listen to them and then replace them with someone else.

original: Where the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, is satisfied, on the information furnished by the mediator or on the information received from any other person including parties to the complaint and after hearing the mediator, it shall replace such mediator by another mediator.
simplification: If the District, State or National Commission is satisfied, based on information from the mediator or from anyone else including the parties to the complaint, and after hearing the mediator, it will replace that mediator with another one.

original: Where the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, is satisfied, on the information furnished by the mediator or on the information received from any other person including parties to the complaint and after hearing the mediator, it shall replace such mediator by another mediator.
simplification: If the District, State or National Commission is satisfied, based on information from the mediator or from some people else including the parties to the complaint, and after hearing the mediator, it will replace that mediator with another one.

simplification: The person picked to help both sides agree has to follow the rules about how and when to do it.

original: The mediator so nominated shall conduct mediation within such time and in such manner as may be specified by regulations.

original: The mediator so nominated shall conduct mediation within such time and in such manner as may be specified by regulations.

simplification: A company that makes a product still has to pay for harm caused, even if it didn't mean to make a false promise.

original: A product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action even if he proves that he was not negligent or fraudulent in making the express warranty of a product.

original: A product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action even if he proves that he was not negligent or fraudulent in making the express warranty of a product.
simplification: A product manufacturer is liable in a product liability case even if it proves that it was careless or dishonest when it gave the express warranty for the product.

original: Any offence punishable under sections 88 and 89, may, either before or after the institution of the prosecution, be compounded, on payment of such amount as may be prescribed: Provided that no compounding of such offence shall be made without the leave of the court before which a complaint has been filed under section 92: Provided further that such sum shall not, in any case, exceed the maximum amount of the fine, which may be imposed under this Act for the offence so compounded.
simplification: Some offences can be settled by paying money instead of going through a full trial. The court has to agree, and the payment can't be more than the biggest fine allowed.

original: Any offence punishable under sections 88 and 89, may, either before or after the institution of the prosecution, be compounded, on payment of such amount as may be prescribed: Provided that no compounding of such offence shall be made without the leave of the court before which a complaint has been filed under section 92: Provided further that such sum shall not, in any case, exceed the maximum amount of the fine, which may be imposed under this Act for the offence so compounded.
simplification: Any offence punishable under sections 88 and 89 can be settled by paying a prescribed amount, either before or after the prosecution starts. However, it cannot be settled without the permission of the court where the complaint was filed under section 92. Also, the amount can never be more than the maximum fine that this Act allows for that offence.

original: Any offence punishable under sections 88 and 89, may, either before or after the institution of the prosecution, be compounded, on payment of such amount as may be prescribed: Provided that no compounding of such offence shall be made without the leave of the court before which a complaint has been filed under section 92: Provided further that such sum shall not, in any case, exceed the maximum amount of the fine, which may be imposed under this Act for the offence so compounded.

original: Where an offence has been compounded under sub-section (1), no proceeding or further proceeding, as the case may be, shall be taken against the offender in respect of the offence so compounded.
simplification: After an offence is settled by paying money, the person can't be taken to court again for it.

original: Where an offence has been compounded under sub-section (1), no proceeding or further proceeding, as the case may be, shall be taken against the offender in respect of the offence so compounded.
simplification: Once an offence has been settled under sub-section (1), no new or further case will be taken against the offender for that offence.

original: Where a notice is served by the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be, under sub-section (1) to a third party in respect of any information or record or part thereof, the third party shall, within ten days from the date of receipt of such notice, be given the opportunity to make representation against the proposed disclosure.
simplification: If the information officer plans to share information about someone else, that person gets 10 days to say why it shouldn't be shared.

original: Where a notice is served by the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be, under sub-section (1) to a third party in respect of any information or record or part thereof, the third party shall, within ten days from the date of receipt of such notice, be given the opportunity to make representation against the proposed disclosure.
simplification: When a Central or State Public Information Officer sends a notice under sub-section (1) to a third party about any information or record, the third party must be given a chance, within ten days of receiving the notice, to object to the planned disclosure.

original: Where a notice is served by the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be, under sub-section (1) to a third party in respect of any information or record or part thereof, the third party shall, within ten days from the date of receipt of such notice, be given the opportunity to make representation against the proposed disclosure.
simplification: When a Central or State Public Information Officer sends a notice under sub-section (1) to a third party about any information or record, the third party must be given a chance, within fifteen days of receiving the notice, to object to the planned disclosure.
